title: Reduce attention kernel memory footprint for multi-tenant GPU pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: FlashAttention (v2/v3) kernels allocate a transient workspace proportional to sequence length and head dims that, in worst-case multi-tenant workloads, causes OOMs or forces cloud autoscaler to move traffic between GPU pools. This ticket aims to reduce per-request ephemeral memory so that a single GPU can host more concurrent tenants without breaking latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce peak ephemeral workspace per attention call by at least 30% across common shapes (seq_len 512..8192).
- Add a guarded allocator path that enforces a per-request kernel memory budget and gracefully falls back to a lower-memory kernel variant when budget exceeded.
- Create regression tests and telemetry to detect memory regressions early in CI and canary.

Non-goals:
- Replace FlashAttention implementation entirely.
- Trade away >10% tail latency increases on p50 workload shapes.

Approach and experiments planned:
1) Workspace reuse: alter runtime's temporary buffer allocator so flash kernels can request a shared per-stream workspace that is reused across microbatches when safe. Expectation: reduce duplicate scratch buffers for prefill + decode phases.
2) Chunked attention path: implement a fallback that computes attention in short-window chunks (overlapping KV) to bound workspace; measure perf delta and memory reduction.
3) Quantized intermediate buffers: for compatibility with v2 layout, evaluate compressing transient floats to FP16/AMP where numeric error is acceptable.
4) Budgeted kernel selector: extend the kernel routing layer to consider an estimated workspace footprint and the per-request memory budget (inferred from tenant and pool config).
5) Regression harness: add CI microbench variants that simulate high tenant density and long-context requests, plus deterministic OOM repro cases captured from staging incidents.
updates: 2026-02-26: Scoping meeting with runtime and infra. Agreed primary path is workspace reuse + budgeted fallback. Collected representative shape distribution from prod (top percentiles: 512, 1024, 2048, 4096).

2026-03-02: Prototyped shared per-stream workspace in local dev; observed 34% reduction in peak ephemeral allocations for seq=2048 on A100 with fa3 kernels when microbatching 4x. Latency delta: +6% p95 in synthetic decode with 8 tokens/sec load. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842 (WIP).

2026-03-04: Discovered regression pattern: when prefill and decode run concurrently on same stream, reuse produced race where kernel returned stale workspace offsets for overlapping requests. Reproduced via unit test harness; introduced per-request arena fencing in prototype to fix correctness. Test case: tests/attn_workspace_race.cc.

2026-03-06: Chunked-attention fallback: implemented naive split-window attention; memory dropped 48% at seq=8192 but throughput dropped by ~22% for encoder-only microbench. Decided to keep as a fallback only when budget threshold exceeded.

2026-03-09: Numerical check on intermediate FP16: for several LLaMA derivatives, FP16 transient buffers produced sub-0.5% perplexity increase on synthetic eval set. Still needs safety review for regression alert thresholds. Added label to track (numerical-risk).

2026-03-11: Canary plan drafted: canary across 2 dedicated pools (low and medium tenant density). Metrics to watch: p50/p95 latency, peak GPU allocation, OOM count, decode success rate, per-tenant tail latency. Canary gating automated via console-telemetry rule. See runbook: https://confluence.redwood/KB/attn-mem-canar y-runbook

2026-03-13: Integration tests green on internal CI with arena fencing and budgeted kernel selector enabled. Microbench results: average peak ephemeral memory reduced 41% for shapes [1024,2048,4096]; p95 latency regression under 9% for worst-case long-context decode. Ready for staged canary rollout.

Nora Kim (runtime) - 2026-03-03: Noted that FlashAttention v3 workspace calc uses temporary 'tiles' array; we can ask the kernel to accept an external workspace pointer. Will experiment with v3 API changes and fallbacks.

next_steps: Complete canary rollout with telemetry gating; add CI OOM regression test; finalize numeric safety signoff with applied-ml; prepare release notes and rollback playbook.
notes: This reduces infrastructure cost by enabling higher tenant packing per GPU pool and prevents noisy OOM-driven autoscaler churn. Keep an eye on FP16 transient degradation for large instruction-following models.
